**My reasoning as this farmer:**

I've been farming in Quzhou my whole life. The land here is flat, the soil is decent — loam, decent water table. Everyone around me grows winter wheat then summer maize on the same fields. My father did it, I do it. It makes sense: wheat goes in October, comes out June, then maize fills the summer. Two crops, one year, same ground. I have about 10 mu total but rent out 2 to my neighbor whose son moved to the city. So I farm 8 mu myself.

For wheat, I'll use the improved Jimai variety the village extension station has been pushing — better yield than the old seed, and I've seen good results on my neighbor's plot. For maize, everyone uses Zhengdan 958 or something similar hybrid from the co-op shop. I wouldn't go back to traditional seed, the hybrid just produces more.

On fertilizer: I put down a base of diammonium phosphate and urea before planting wheat, then topdress with urea at jointing. I know the county agronomist said we use too much nitrogen, but I'd rather not risk a bad harvest. I water three times for wheat — before winter freeze, at jointing, at heading. Maize I rely on summer rain mostly, maybe water once if July is dry.

Maize I'll direct-seed after wheat harvest. No ploughing — saves fuel, saves time, and the soil is fine.
